JAFF Market, which organizers bill as Indonesia’s biggest film market, opened its third edition at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta with market director Linda Gozali urging the local industry to judge its growth on quality as well as scale.

Gozali said the first edition was conceived as an experiment. “It is actually a question that we threw into the Indonesian ecosystem whether or not we truly need a film market. Gozali said the market’s third outing called for some reflection on whether the industry can “actually endure and survive the economic upheaval, the socio-political instability, as well as whatever issues that are actually evolving in the global era.”

The 2025 edition centered on local and international collaboration, she said, with the goal of turning leads into multiple deals.

“This is a transitional period, and therefore let’s define what growth is,” Gozali added. “We have to define growth not just in terms of the quantity, no. Because growth in quantity itself will reduce at a time where there are challenges around the environment. So we look at growth as well from the quality point of view.”

JAFF Market, which organizers bill as Indonesia’s biggest film market, opened its third edition at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta with market director Linda Gozali urging the local industry to judge its growth on quality as well as scale.

The three-day market runs alongside the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF). Gozali said the first edition was conceived as an experiment. “It is actually a question that we threw into the Indonesian ecosystem whether or not we truly need a film market. And the response was definitely overwhelming,” she said.

Gozali said the market’s third outing called for some reflection on whether the industry can “actually endure and survive the economic upheaval, the socio-political instability, as well as whatever issues that are actually evolving in the global era.”

The 2025 edition centered on local and international collaboration, she said, with the goal of turning leads into multiple deals.

“This is a transitional period, and therefore let’s define what growth is,” Gozali added. “We have to define growth not just in terms of the quantity, no. Because growth in quantity itself will reduce at a time where there are challenges around the environment. So we look at growth as well from the quality point of view.”
